paper.title: Gaussian Process Optimization with Mutual Information

settings.name_in_paper: Sequential optimization of f sampled from a Gaussian process with noisy observations (GP optimization)
unmapped: f is a sample from a zero-mean GP with known kernel k, k(x,x) <= 1
X subset R^d compact and convex
regret is a high-probability bound over the GP prior draw and noise (Bayesian high-probability regret)
settings.definition_quote: Let $f:\X \to \R$, where $\X \subset \R^d$ is a compact and convex set ... $y_t = f(x_t)+\epsilon_t$ ... noise variables ... $\N(0,\sigma^2)$ ... we assume that $f$ is sampled from a Gaussian process $\mathcal{GP}(m, k)$ ... $k(x,x)\leq 1$

algorithms.name: Generic scheme with phi_t(x) = sqrt(alpha)/2 sigma_t^2(x) (GP-UCB variant with fixed exploration)

symbols.Sigma_star: sum_t sigma_t^2(x*), posterior variances at the optimum

conditions: f drawn from GP with kernel k(x,x)<=1

source.label: thm:general_regret
source.quote: For all $\delta>0$ and $T>0$, the regret $R_T$ incurred by Algorithm \ref{alg:gpopt} on $f$ distributed as a GP perturbed by independent Gaussian noise with variance $\sigma^2$ satisfies ... $\Pr[ R_T \leq \sum_{t=1}^T (\phi_t(x_t) -\phi_t(x^\star)) + 4\sqrt{\alpha (C_1\gamma_T+1)} + \frac{\sqrt{\alpha}}{2}\frac{\sum_{t=1}^T \sigma_t^2(x^\star)}{\sqrt{C_1\gamma_T+1}} ] \geq 1-\delta$.

results.notes: Authors' erratum states Lemma 1 (martingale claim) is wrong, invalidating the main theorem; they exhibit cases of linear regret for GP-MI. Recorded as stated.

source.label: cor:gpucb
source.quote: Consider the Algorithm \ref{alg:gpopt} where we set $\phi_t(x) = \frac{\sqrt{\alpha}}{2} \sigma_t^2(x)$. ... For $f$ sampled from a GP with general kernel: $R_T = \O(\gamma_T)$.

results.notes: Explicit form in text: R_T <= sqrt(alpha)/2 C_1 gamma_T + 4 sqrt(alpha(C_1 gamma_T+1)) w.p. 1-delta. Invalidated per authors' erratum.

source.label: cor:gpucb
source.quote: For $f$ sampled from a GP with RBF kernel: $R_T = \O\big( (\log T)^{d+1} \big)$.

results.notes: Text also states O(d log T) for linear kernel. Invalidated per authors' erratum.

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: For all $\delta>0$ and $T>1$, the regret $R_T$ incurred by Algorithm \ref{alg:gpmi} on $f$ distributed as a GP perturbed by independent Gaussian noise with variance $\sigma^2$ satisfies ... $\Pr\Big[R_T \leq 5\sqrt{\alpha C_1 \gamma_T} + 4\sqrt{\alpha} \Big] \geq 1-\delta$.

results.notes: Lemma 5 restates this. The authors' erratum states the proof is wrong and GP-MI can incur linear regret; the result is invalid as stated.

source.label: cor:rbf_gpmi
source.quote: The cumulative regret $R_T$ incurred by Algorithm \ref{alg:gpmi} on $f$ sampled from a GP with RBF kernel satisfies with high probability, $R_T = \O\Big((\log T)^{\frac{d+1}{2}}\Big)$.
